% [MAIN 2]
\begin{table}[tbp]
  \centering
  \small
  \caption{\textbf{The metric battery.} Ten measurements of the same edge. Metric~1 defines the candidate set and 2--7 grade it. Metric~2a is named honestly as a \emph{contribution filter} rather than as Tree SAE's $S_\mathrm{res}$: two strong but unrelated co-firing features pass both of its legs, and its pass rate scales with block energy. The probe-based $S_\mathrm{res}$ is 2b, and its target is the self-label $\mathbf{1}[f_c > 0]$, so a corrupted latent yields a probe that validates its own corruption; we report it as self-labeled and as a self-consistency check, not as ground truth.}
  \label{tab:battery}
  \begin{tabular}{llllr}
    \toprule
     & Metric & What it asks & Threshold & Module \\
    \midrule
    1a & Reverse coverage $R$ & $P(\text{parent} \mid \text{child})$ & $\geq 0.5$ & \texttt{coverage} \\
    1b & Forward coverage $F$ & $P(\text{child} \mid \text{parent})$ & reported & \texttt{coverage} \\
    1c & Joint-child coverage & $R_\mathrm{supp}$, $R_\mathrm{mass}$, energy share & reported & \texttt{joint\_child} \\
    2a & Reconstruction ablation & both features carry mass on the child's tokens & $\geq 0.01$ & \texttt{reconstruction} \\
    2b & Probe $S_\mathrm{res}$ & both decoders near the child-concept probe & top-5 rank & \texttt{sres} \\
    3 & Sibling redundancy & co-activation among one parent's children & $\geq 0.5$ & \texttt{sibling\_redundancy} \\
    4 & Out-degree & one parent covering most of the next block & $\geq 30\%$ & \texttt{outdegree} \\
    5 & Token-frequency control & does the edge survive on rare tokens & $\geq 0.5$ & \texttt{token\_control} \\
    6 & Independence null & PMI against independent firing & $> 0$ & \texttt{independence\_null} \\
    7 & In-block directed coverage & containment within one block, and duplicates & asymmetry & \texttt{in\_block\_edges} \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
\end{table}

\begin{table}[tbp]

  \caption{\textbf{What each metric can separate.} A candidate pair can look like an edge for seven reasons and only one is hierarchy, so the question per metric is which column it adds, not whether it is correct. $\bullet$ detects, $\circ$ partial (necessary but not sufficient, or only in some regimes), -- blind. \textbf{These cells are read off each metric's construction and are not a measured accuracy}; every one is exercised by a row of Table~\ref{tab:tier1}. Two columns are open and stay open. \emph{Absorption} is unreachable because coverage gates the candidate set and an absorbed child has low $R$ by construction. \emph{Topic} --- two specific, unrelated features sharing a latent subject --- passes coverage, reconstruction, the frequency control and PMI alike; closing it needs a model-based topic null rather than another threshold.}

    4 Out-degree & -- & -- & -- & $\bullet$ & -- & $\circ$ & -- \\

% [MAIN 4]
\begin{table}[tbp]
  \centering
  \small
  \caption{\textbf{Three tiers, trading ground truth against realism.} Each rung licenses the one above it. Tier~1 proves the arithmetic and nothing about whether an SAE would learn such a structure; Tier~2 closes exactly that gap, because only what the SAE actually learned reaches the metrics, which is also what lets it attribute a miss --- a missed edge counts against a metric only if the SAE learned both endpoints. Tier~3 has no known answer and is named for how it is judged rather than what it runs on.}
  \label{tab:tiers}
  \begin{tabular}{llll}
    \toprule
    Tier & Runs on & Ground truth & Result \\
    \midrule
    1 Synthetic toy & hand-built statistics & by construction & 14/14 rows, 21/21 functions, seeds 0--7 \\
    2 Trained toy & a Matryoshka SAE trained on that tree & the tree is known & precision 1.00, recall 0.67 \\
    3 Real SAE & \texttt{google/gemma-2-2b} & none --- human reading & 40 survivors read against autointerp labels \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
  \\[2pt] \footnotesize Lateral control (not a tier): 6/6 testable true edges run early block $\rightarrow$ late on the trained toy.
\end{table}

% [APP 2]
\begin{table}[tbp]
  \centering
  \small
  \caption{\textbf{The rank rule's null depends on dictionary size.} $S_\mathrm{res}$ passes an edge when both decoders fall in the top $k = 5$ of the probe's correlations over the whole dictionary. It is a geometry test, so an unrelated parent passes whenever chance puts it there, at a rate of $k/D$. The same $k$ is therefore two orders of magnitude stricter on gemma than on a 42-feature toy, and a measured pass rate is only interpretable against its own null: two runs on the \emph{same} 1{,}792-latent dictionary land on opposite sides of theirs. Reporting $S_\mathrm{res}$ shares across sources without this correction compares nothing.}
  \label{tab:null}
  \begin{tabular}{lrrrr}
    \toprule
    Source & $D$ & Null $k/D$ & Observed & vs.\ null \\
    \midrule
    Synthetic toy (Tier 1) & 42 & 11.9\% & --- & --- \\
    Trained toy (Tier 2) & 20 & 25.0\% & 5/5 true edges & --- \\
    \texttt{gemma-2-2b} L6 & 32,768 & 0.015\% & 0.59\% & 39$\times$ \\
    PCFG layer 01 & 1,792 & 0.279\% & 0.00\% & below chance \\
    PCFG layer 03 & 1,792 & 0.279\% & 0.52\% & 2$\times$ \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
\end{table}

% [APP 3]
\begin{table}[tbp]
  \centering
  \small
  \caption{\textbf{One contaminating token position moved five of six metrics.} Means over the five graded layers, block pair B0$\rightarrow$B1, before and after excluding the beginning-of-sequence position. BOS is an attention sink on which effectively every feature fires; with 400 documents it gave every pair in the dictionary 400 joint firings against a support guard of $\mathrm{MIN\_JOINT} = 30$, so the guard admitted pairs that never co-occur anywhere else. Every quantity computed from that one co-firing matrix moved, and the one that is not --- a ratio over children that already have a parent --- did not. \textbf{The \emph{before} column is withdrawn} and is reproduced only to size the error. Agreement among detectors that share an input is much weaker evidence than a battery implies.}
  \label{tab:bos}
  \begin{tabular}{lrrrr}
    \toprule
    Quantity & Reads co-fire & Before & After & Change \\
    \midrule
    Candidate edges & \checkmark & 4,865 & 1,855 & 0.38$\times$ \\
    Improve reconstruction, \% & \checkmark & 18 & 76 & 4.19$\times$ \\
    Frequency-driven, \% & \checkmark & 50.3 & 1.5 & 0.03$\times$ \\
    Mean frequency survival & \checkmark & 0.54 & 1.01 & 1.87$\times$ \\
    Sibling redundancy & \checkmark & 0.31 & 0.05 & 0.16$\times$ \\
    Superparents flagged & \checkmark & 7.6 & 4.2 & 0.55$\times$ \\
    Children with $\geq 2$ parents, \% & -- & 99 & 97 & 0.99$\times$ \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
\end{table}
